Name: Tenkai Harem Love - Private Spouse Suites SVE
Author: TENKAITENSHI
Description:
Tenkai Harem Love — Private Spouse Suites
[b]Give every spouse a home that feels like theirs.[/b]
Tenkai Harem Love adds an upstairs gallery leading to separate, personalized spouse suites. Each partner receives their own bedroom, furniture and hobby space, while you remain free to redecorate using Stardew Valley’s normal furniture controls.
The gallery grows with your household, creating space for additional marriages without placing every spouse in the same shared bedroom.
[heading]Choose your version: 1.9 or 1.10[/heading]
[b]Version 1.9 — The original spouse suites[/b]
Version 1.9 focuses on Stardew Valley’s [b]12 original marriage candidates[/b], with individual room styles, native movable furniture, wedding portraits, hobby areas and household features.
This is the original edition for players who want Harem Love’s suites without the additional Stardew Valley Expanded content. It includes [b]41 exclusive furniture IDs[/b].
[b]Version 1.10 — Optional Stardew Valley Expanded integration[/b]
Version 1.10 builds on the original suite system and adds dedicated support for [b]seven additional marriage candidates available through Stardew Valley Expanded[/b]:
[b]Claire, Sophia, Olivia, Victor, Lance, Scarlett and Magnus.[/b]
Each receives a personalized suite, themed furnishings, a wedding portrait and an activity area reflecting their interests. This version also adds compatibility adjustments for additional-spouse conditions, events and work or travel schedules.
[b]You can use version 1.10 without SVE.[/b] Stardew Valley Expanded remains optional: its additional suite themes become available when the expansion is installed. Installing Harem Love does not install SVE, introduce its characters into your world or bypass their progression requirements.

[heading]What the mod does[/heading]
[list]
[*]Creates a private suite for each recognized marriage and extends the upstairs gallery as the household grows.[/*]
[*]Gives the 12 original marriage candidates their own colors, furnishings and interests.[/*]
[*]Uses real Stardew Valley furniture that you can pick up, carry, store in a chest, remove and place again.[/*]
[*]Allows you to add furniture and wall decorations purchased in the game.[/*]
[*]Connects spouse activities to the furniture currently present in their suite.[/*]
[*]Includes wedding portraits and short, inspectable stories for selected objects and keepsakes.[/*]
[*]Handles spouse-room returns, sleeping positions, household movement, kisses and partner-aware family features.[/*]
[*]Provides English and Spanish text automatically through the game’s language setting.[/*]
[/list][heading]The original spouse suites[/heading]
The original candidates retain their individual room designs.
[b]Abigail[/b] has an animated amethyst waterfall, a terrarium, gaming furniture and an adventuring atmosphere. Her gaming furniture also includes a playable interaction.
[b]Haley[/b] has a photography studio, a vanity, wedding memories and a space for exercise and relaxation.
[b]Penny[/b] has a reading and teaching space, including a specially designed desk and library furnishings.
[b]Leah[/b] has an artist’s workshop, carving furniture and a sculpture activity area.
The other original marriage candidates also receive their own room palettes, furnishings and decorations inspired by their interests.
[heading]New in 1.10: Stardew Valley Expanded suites[/heading]
The Expanded integration adds seven complete room themes, with personalized walls, floors, trim, beds, doors, windows and furnishing arrangements.
[b]Claire — Ballet and quiet comforts[/b]
A gentle room with a ballet rehearsal corner, mirror and barre, plus a tea cabinet for quieter moments at home.
[b]Sophia — Manga, cosplay and vineyard memories[/b]
A colorful personal space combining manga, costume projects and keepsakes connected to her life at the vineyard.
[b]Olivia — Wine and art[/b]
An elegant suite with a wine cabinet, art displays and refined furnishings.
[b]Victor — Engineering and design[/b]
A study inspired by technical drawing and construction, with a drafting workstation and a miniature bridge display.
[b]Lance — Expeditions and discoveries[/b]
A room for an adventurer, with expedition equipment, maps and a collection of unusual relics.
[b]Scarlett — Creativity and travel[/b]
A warm creative space with a costume-making workstation, sewing details and travel keepsakes.
[b]Magnus — Alchemy and astronomy[/b]
An arcane suite with an alchemy cabinet, books, potions and celestial instruments.
These additions include [b]14 newly created furniture pieces and seven framed wedding portraits[/b], with English and Spanish names and object stories.
[heading]Decorating your suites[/heading]
Use the game’s normal furniture controls. There is no F2 room editor or custom white selection frame.
Pick up furniture, carry it in your inventory, store it in a chest and place it wherever the normal placement rules allow. You can also bring purchased decorations into the suites.
Your changes are saved with the game. Removed objects do not automatically respawn, and relocated furniture keeps its saved position.
Spouse activities follow their corresponding furniture. Moving a workstation moves its activity anchor; removing it stops that activity until a suitable object returns.
[b]Tenkai Safe Decorating is optional.[/b] With version 1.1.0 or later, its configured toggle—F7 by default—locks and unlocks suite furniture using the same protection applied to normal house furniture.
Version 1.10 also corrects Harem’s adventure sword to occupy [b]two wall tiles[/b]. Existing Harem-marked swords are updated while retaining their placement and ownership information.
[heading]SVE progression, events and schedules[/heading]
SVE continues to provide its characters, quests, story progression and unlock requirements.
Harem’s integration recognizes additional spouses in supported marriage conditions while preserving the expansion’s other requirements. Adding a suite theme does not automatically unlock a character, grant friendship, complete a quest or create a marriage.
Active SVE work and travel schedules retain control outside the home, including Lance’s overnight absences. Harem also suspends its household goal updates during events.
[b]Apples remains SVE’s nonromantic roommate[/b] and is not included among these seven romance suites.
[heading]Original downstairs spouse room[/heading]
The original downstairs spouse room loads normally. The old Harem-specific removal marker no longer closes it.
Robin’s purchased renovations remain under the game’s control. Furniture previously recovered to a chest stays wherever the player placed it.
[heading]Marriage providers and other room mods[/heading]
Harem reads marriages from the save and includes its own additional-proposal handling.
It recognizes [b]Free Love, legacy Multiple Spouses and PolyamorySweet Love[/b], and defers additional-proposal handling when one of those providers is installed. This recognition does not confirm that every feature of those mods works together.
Room-building modules are a separate consideration. [b]Custom Spouse Rooms[/b] and [b]PolyamorySweet Rooms[/b] can generate competing rooms.
Before switching room providers:
[list=1]
[*]Back up your save.[/*]
[*]Move belongings out of areas that the previous provider will remove.[/*]
[*]Close the game and disable that provider’s room-building function.[/*]
[*]Restart and inspect the farmhouse before saving.[/*]
[/list]Harem warns about known competing room builders. It does not automatically delete their rooms, configurations or belongings. Read [b]COMPATIBILITY.txt[/b] before combining them.
[heading]Installation[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Back up the save you intend to use.[/*]
[*]Install SMAPI and launch the game through it.[/*]
[*]With the game closed, extract the [b]HaremLove[/b] folder into [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b].[/*]
[*]When upgrading, preserve your existing [b]config.json[/b] and [b]data[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]If you want the Expanded suites, install [b]Stardew Valley Expanded and its required dependencies separately[/b].[/*]
[*]Restart through SMAPI, load your save and check the upstairs access.[/*]
[/list]Use [b]harem_info[/b] in the SMAPI console to see detected marriages, suites, access information and the status of the SVE integration.
The first load of a pre-1.8 layout converts its room decorations into native furniture once. Existing layout coordinates and purchased furniture are retained.
[heading]Public beta and verification[/heading]
This is a [b]public beta[/b].
The version 1.10 verification target was:
[list]
[*]Windows[/*]
[*]Stardew Valley [b]1.6.15[/b][/*]
[*]SMAPI [b]4.5.2[/b][/*]
[*]Stardew Valley Expanded [b]1.15.11[/b][/*]
[*]Content Patcher [b]2.9.1[/b][/*]
[*]Farm Type Manager [b]1.26.1[/b][/*]
[/list]Testing included isolated game sessions with and without SVE, native furniture placement and storage, spouse activities, kisses, room returns, full saving and an independent reload of the saved copy. The reload checks confirmed that the seven SVE spouses remained present and moved workstations retained their positions without duplicating.
Screenshots were captured inside an isolated demonstration copy.
These checks do not represent a complete playthrough of every heart event, wedding or birth scenario. [b]Multiplayer, split screen, other operating systems, heavily modified farmhouse maps and every third-party add-on combination remain unverified.[/b] Other custom NPCs do not automatically receive the same hand-designed artwork as the supported original and SVE candidates.
[heading]Upgrading, removal and rollback[/heading]
Custom furniture IDs become part of the save after saving.
Restoring only an older DLL does not restore objects introduced by a newer version. Keep a matching earlier save if you need to revert or remove the mod, especially when returning from 1.10 to a version without its new furniture IDs.
Test major updates on a copy first.
[heading]Credits and artwork[/heading]
Created by [b]Tenkai Tenshi[/b].
Bespoke furniture and wedding artwork were made with AI assistance and adapted for this project’s pixel-art presentation.
Stardew Valley and its original characters and assets belong to [b]ConcernedApe[/b]. Stardew Valley Expanded and its added characters belong to [b]FlashShifter and the SVE contributors[/b].
Base-game artwork is referenced at runtime. Original SVE artwork, game files, SMAPI and other mods are not bundled with this download.
[heading]Reporting an issue[/heading]
Please include:
[list]
[*]Your Harem Love version.[/*]
[*]Your game and SMAPI versions.[/*]
[*]Your SVE version, if installed.[/*]
[*]Relevant marriage, room, schedule or family mods.[/*]
[*]A SMAPI log and clear reproduction steps.[/*]
[*]Screenshots when the problem involves placement, animation or appearance.[/*]
[/list]For furniture issues, mention whether the item was an original suite object, a purchased decoration or a catalog replacement, and whether it was moved before the issue appeared.
